title: pvAMRGaussianPulseSource
body:
## pvAMRGaussianPulseSource

Generates a small synthetic overlapping AMR dataset (vtkOverlappingAMR) with two levels: a root block of 6 × 6 (× 6) points starting at (-2, -2, 0) with spacing RootSpacing, plus two refined patches. Cell arrays are "Gaussian-Pulse" = PulseAmplitude · exp(-Σ((x - origin)/width)²) and "Centroid". Use it to test AMR pipelines and readers (compare with pvXMLUniformGridAMRReader); it is not physical data.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- The pulse origin and width are in the same coordinates as the grid; with the default spacing 0.5 the root block spans only [-2, 0.5] in x and y, so a pulse placed far outside is invisible.
- Schemaxis generates this source from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for it, so inspect the output before relying on it.

Native constructor: `AMRGaussianPulseSource`. Identity: `sources/AMRGaussianPulseSource`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Dimension` | Sets the desired dimension for the AMR dataset to generate. | `{"type":"enum","values":["2D","3D"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"2D"` |
| `PulseAmplitude` | Sets the amplitude of the pulse | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":0.0001,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.0001` |
| `RefinementRatio` | Factor by which the cell size shrinks from the root level to the refined level: with 2, each refined cell is half the root cell size in every direction. Larger ratios give finer patches and more cells. The native documentation repeats the Dimension text by mistake. | `{"type":"enum","values":["2","3","4"]}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"2"` |
| `RootSpacing` | Set the spacing at level 0. | `{"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `1` |
| `XPulseOrigin` | Set x-coordinate for the pulse origin | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":-1.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `-1.0` |
| `XPulseWidth` | Width of the Gaussian pulse along x: the distance from the pulse centre at which the value drops to 1/e of the amplitude along that axis. Larger widths give a broader, smoother pulse. The native wording "x-coordinate for the pulse Width" is misleading. | `{"maximum":10.0,"minimum":0.5,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.5` |
| `YPulseOrigin` | Set y-coordinate for the pulse origin | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":-1.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `-1.0` |
| `YPulseWidth` | Width of the Gaussian pulse along y: the distance from the pulse centre at which the value drops to 1/e of the amplitude along that axis. Larger widths give a broader, smoother pulse. The native wording "x-coordinate for the pulse Width" is misleading. | `{"maximum":10.0,"minimum":0.5,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.5` |
| `ZPulseOrigin` | Set z-coordinate for the pulse origin | `{"maximum":1.0,"minimum":-1.0,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `-1.0` |
| `ZPulseWidth` | Width of the Gaussian pulse along z: the distance from the pulse centre at which the value drops to 1/e of the amplitude along that axis. Larger widths give a broader, smoother pulse. Used only for 3D output. The native wording "x-coordinate for the pulse Width" is misleading. | `{"maximum":10.0,"minimum":0.5,"type":"number"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `0.5` |
